topic: Work Done by a Variable Force
title: Which F? Work by a Variable Force Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
Stretch a rubber band, pull a spring, draw back a bow string: the further you pull, the harder it pulls back. Aarav stretches a band by 10 cm and it ends up pulling with 20 N. So how much work did he do? W = F d, but which F? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) we learn how to find the work done by a force that keeps changing.

A live simulation stretches the band while its force graph draws beside it. We cut the stretch into 4, then 10, then 40 thin strips and watch the estimate climb from 0.75 J to 0.9 J to 0.975 J, settling at exactly 1 J, with a slow-mo replay of one strip. Then we build W = integral of F dx step by step and see why work is the area under the F-x graph, compare two pulls side by side, explain link by link why area below the axis is negative work, and split a graph into simple shapes in a worked example. Then the exam trap about averaging forces, an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for NCERT, CBSE, ISC and PUC Class 11 students, and for JEE Main and NEET.
